title: Mosby's San Francisco Apex and returning to the Cotton Club
summary: The San Francisco Apex was on upper floors near Chinatown; Brown went in and out between Mosby and the Cotton Club, replacing Lewis Taylor.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You mentioned that when you were with Curtis Mosby at the Apex in Los Angeles, that you would sometimes go to San Francisco to play a show.
Whereabouts in San Francisco did you play with Mosby?

Well, Mosby set up two clubs, one in San Francisco, and one in Los Angeles. And this club in San Francisco was kind of on the second and third floor in a building -- it was right at the beginning of Chinatown. I more or less think it was on Bush and between -- let me see. What were those streets up in there. Between Grant and Kearney. Right there. I think it was Bush Street. It was a north and south street it was on.
But it was up on a second and third floor right down in town, and it was very popular because it was a new type of thing. And its situation down town among all the hotels, why it did quite well.
And that club they called the Apex also?
The Apex, yes. San Francisco Apex.
We've sort of jumped back and forth from the Apex to the Cotton Club but -- so I'm not quite certain how long you were with Curtis Mosby. How long did you

Well, it was a few months. I don't remember too much because between the times at Curtis' place, we would do many some dances, and then we'd go down to Los Angeles and go back in the Cotton Club, and in and out and around like that. It's kind of hard to remember back as far as 1928, and '29.
But you played at the Cotton Club until you went with Mosby, and then you left Mosby to go back to the Cotton Club, is that right?

Right, they changed bands, and as I said before, Lionel Hampton and I had contracts with the Cotton Club, not with the bands that came there. We -- we went in and out, and most of the time stayed regardless of who came.
And when you first went into the Cotton Club you said that you were replacing a trombone player who had left and that his name was Taylor. I didn't get his first name.

I think it was Lewis Taylor. He was a boy from Chicago, and I think he was sick and he had to leave the west coast and go back to Chicago. And that gave me a chance to join that band. At that time it was called the Quality Serenaders, Uh-huh.
